items.headline: US outages hit NSA classified network, Apple, FAA and banks; officials see no cyberattack
items.summary: A run of US outages since 12 Nov hit the NSA's internal network, Apple services, FAA air traffic systems, Chase and Microsoft 365. Officials say no evidence of attack or coordination; causes cited include maintenance, a router failure and an update.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: NSA, Apple, FAA and Chase acknowledged outages; officials deny cyberattack evidence. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: Tuesday 17 November 2026, CNN exclusive on NSA network (evening UK); Apple/NSA statements same day

sections.happened: Since 12 November, outages have affected Microsoft 365, the FAA (nationwide ground stop), United Airlines, JPMorgan Chase and Zelle. On 17 November the NSA's classified internal network went down, and Apple Music, App Store, AppleCare and iCloud sign-in failed. Marriott and Schwab also reported problems. The NSA said mission-critical capabilities stayed operational. Apple cited an internal update.
sections.technical: No cyber vector has been identified. Stated causes: NSA, 'temporary degradation' during scheduled maintenance (Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton reportedly said a patch for vulnerabilities); FAA, a failed router, root cause undetermined per Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy; Apple, an internal update; Chase, a technical issue it said was not an attack.
sections.guidance: ISC2 chief operating officer Casey Marks said organisations should identify the systems and vendors they cannot operate without, then test what happens when those services go down.
sections.differing: Officials (Rubio, Clayton, Mullin) say there is no sign of coordination or state action; some commentators cite AI-driven patching pressure. FAA's Bedford called AI speculation unfounded. The better-supported view is isolated failures, though FAA root cause is open.
sections.unknown: FAA router root cause, the full NSA outage cause and duration, and whether any outages share a common factor remain undetermined.

items.headline: Russian group COLD RELIC uses one cloud breach to pivot into another
items.summary: Google GTIG and Mandiant report Russian espionage group COLD RELIC (Star Blizzard) used a stolen super admin account, then impersonation, to breach a second US organisation via Entra ID SSO.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Google GTIG/Mandiant report; primary page unreadable, details from secondary coverage. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 (Google Cloud blog, dated 17 November 2026); first press coverage 18 Nov 2026

sections.happened: Google GTIG and Mandiant describe two linked intrusions at US organisations: a late-2025 super admin takeover with MFA fatigue, then a 2026 Entra ID SSO compromise via impersonation. Attribution to COLD RELIC is stated as high confidence.
sections.technical: Residential proxy near victim, MFA push fatigue, super admin bulk Drive download and Takeout export, Alert Center deletion, rogue MFA devices and passkeys, OAuth email sync, hijacked sessions surviving password resets. Cited ATT&CK T1562.008 and T1082.
sections.guidance: Google recommends proxy/VPN reputation enrichment of auth logs, conditional access against known proxies, cloud DLP, revoking all sessions and forcing resets, phishing-resistant MFA, and restricting passkey registration.
sections.unknown: Affected organisations, data volume and downstream victims were not named. Primary Google page could not be read; the DOJ FSB link is from prior legal actions.

items.headline: Equinor reports ongoing cyberattack on IT systems; production unaffected
items.summary: Equinor detected an ongoing cyberattack on certain IT systems on 17 November. It says production is normal and no data theft is indicated. Internal email was reportedly down. The attack is still ongoing as of 19 November; no actor named.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Equinor's own statements, corroborated by The Record, Reuters-cited reports and NSM.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 17:55 UK (18:55 CET), Equinor company statement

sections.happened: Equinor said at 18:55 CET on 17 November that it had detected an ongoing cyberattack against certain IT systems, with production unaffected. On 18 November it said it was not a virus attack and would not spread. On 19 November it said the attack was still ongoing, could not give a time to restore systems, had reported it to police, and that the attack did not appear specifically aimed at Equinor. Employees reportedly had trouble accessing applications; Reuters cited a source saying internal email was down.
sections.technical: Equinor says the attack is not a virus attack. It has not disclosed the access vector, affected systems, malware or IOCs, and no ATT&CK techniques or CVEs have been published. No actor has been named or has claimed the attack.
sections.guidance: None published beyond Equinor saying it is working with national security authorities and has informed police. Norway's NSM said it was aware and ready to support.
sections.unknown: Attacker, access method, which systems are affected, restoration timeline, and why Equinor says the attack does not appear to target it specifically.

items.headline: European Commission confirms AI-assisted cyberattack that took HR and other systems offline
items.summary: The Commission confirmed on 19 November a cyber campaign detected 22 October that used publicly available AI tools. Several applications were taken offline and mostly restored. Politico reported ARTEX use; the Commission has not named the tool, attacker or any data loss.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Commission spokesperson confirmed incident and AI tool use at press briefing. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 19 November 2026, Politico (per The Record and Infosecurity Magazine); Commission confirmed same day

sections.happened: Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said on 19 November that the first signs of an attack were detected on 22 October and it was confirmed as a cyber-attack on 26 October. Several applications were temporarily taken down as a protective measure and most have been restored. Politico reported affected systems included Sysper (HR) and medical reimbursements; The Record reported disruption of over 10 days. The EDPS and CERT-EU are involved. The Commission is not aware of a ransom demand and has found no evidence of a data breach affecting staff. It is the third disclosed incident this year.
sections.technical: Regnier confirmed the campaign was AI-generated using a publicly available tool, without naming it. Politico, as reported by others, said CERT-EU identified ARTEX, an open-source LLM-driven penetration-testing framework. CERT-EU's 5 November blog said AI-driven activity against its constituency 'highly likely' involved ARTEX. The FBI flash of 13 November reported some intrusions reaching privileged access in under three hours. No CVE, vector or actor has been published for the Commission incident.
sections.guidance: CERT-EU's 5 November post recommends regular vulnerability scans and penetration tests of internet-facing devices, and keeping all findings, including non-severe ones, in the remediation cycle so tooling cannot chain minor misconfigurations.
sections.differing: Politico, via secondary reports, said ARTEX was used and personal data may have been breached. The Commission confirmed only AI tools and says it has no evidence of a staff data breach; the investigation continues.
sections.unknown: Attacker identity, motive, entry point, whether ARTEX specifically was used, and whether any data was accessed remain undisclosed.

items.headline: Rakuten Securities says test-environment breach may have exposed data on up to 15.72 million accounts
items.summary: Rakuten Securities reported unauthorised access to a test environment holding real customer data. Up to 4.47m accounts may have lost personal and financial details; 11.25m more may have lost IDs. Passwords and PINs reportedly not taken; no fraudulent trades found.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: Independent verification did not run for this top story, so the label is lowered; details come from the cited reports.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 (UK time unconfirmed): Rakuten Securities notice, as reported by Infosecurity Magazine

sections.happened: Rakuten Securities, part of Rakuten Group, said it detected possible unauthorised access on 16 November and cut off access. It found that information in a test environment may have been leaked externally on 11 November. It published an apology on 17 November. Up to 4.47 million accounts may have had names, addresses, employer, bank details, income and asset data exposed; a further 11.25 million may have had branch/customer codes and login IDs exposed. Jiji reports a combined 15.72 million, including closed accounts. The company postponed a Shibuya branch opening and waived fund-transfer fees.
sections.technical: Vector and attacker are not disclosed; the company says cause and circumstances are under investigation. The test environment normally holds dummy data, but real customer data was present. A company spokesperson, cited by ASCII.jp, said production data was needed to verify an internal system update. Mallory.ai asserts an undisclosed vulnerability was exploited; this is not in the company notice as reported.
sections.guidance: Rakuten Securities said it will contact affected customers individually, is making passkey login mandatory, and urged customers to set up passkeys, use its temporary trading and withdrawal suspension setting, and beware suspicious emails, texts and calls.
sections.unknown: Attack method, attacker identity, why five days passed before detection, and whether data was actually exfiltrated (company says only 'may have').

items.headline: Wellington IT attack exposes payee data at around 40 Irish credit unions
items.summary: An October attack on Belfast-based software provider Wellington IT exposed saved payee details at about 40 Irish credit unions; a minister criticised the late notification.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Wellington IT confirmed a security incident; credit unions and minister confirmed; details still under investigation. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: Tue 18 Nov 2026, Irish media (RTÉ, Irish Independent); The Register 11:45 UTC 19 Nov

sections.happened: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in Wellington IT's CU Online banking platform between 2 and 4 October 2026; the flaw was closed on 6 October. Credit unions were notified only in mid-November. Exposed saved payee records, not login credentials, at about 40 Irish credit unions, per minister Robert Troy.
sections.technical: Per notices seen by the Irish Examiner: an automated script made five million requests exploiting an authorisation flaw, using valid credentials. Wellington IT says it lacks activity logs to confirm which member data was taken.
sections.guidance: Credit unions advise members to be wary of unexpected calls, texts or emails, not to transfer money on anyone's claim it must be moved for safety, and never to share PINs or login details.
sections.differing: Troy said the company notified credit unions only after confirming risk; Wellington IT says it alerted customers 'as soon as' it confirmed risk. Request counts differ: five million (Irish Examiner via BleepingComputer) versus 1.4 million (Clare Echo).
sections.unknown: Total number of affected members (reports range to hundreds of thousands); full scope of data; whether other Wellington IT clients are affected; the attacker is unidentified.

items.headline: Gentlemen ransomware lists NVIDIA on leak site; NVIDIA cites possible third-party partner incident
items.summary: The Gentlemen ransomware group listed NVIDIA on its leak site with a roughly 10-day countdown but no sample data. NVIDIA says it found no indication its own systems or networks were affected and is investigating a possible partner incident.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: Group listing without evidence; NVIDIA reports no sign its systems were affected.
items.firstReported: 18-19 Nov 2026 (UK time not stated); SecurityWeek and iThome

sections.happened: The Gentlemen ransomware group added NVIDIA to its dark-web leak site on 18 November 2026, according to secondary reports. iThome reports a countdown of about 10 days before stolen data would be published. The listing gives a company description and Tox contact details, but no data types, samples or intrusion date. NVIDIA told SecurityWeek it is investigating an incident that may have affected a third-party partner and has found no indication its systems or networks were affected.
sections.technical: No technical details of the alleged intrusion have been published. SecurityWeek says the group, tracked by Microsoft as Storm-2697, uses double extortion. It cites Sophos as saying affiliates used compromised credentials and legitimate administrative tools, with ransomware deployed in under 24 hours in one case. The leak site reportedly lists over 1,100 alleged victims. No CVEs or IOCs for this claim.
sections.differing: The group implies NVIDIA data was taken. NVIDIA reports no sign its own systems were affected and points to a third-party partner. No evidence has been published, so the NVIDIA position is better supported for now.
sections.unknown: Whether any data exists, whose it is, the partner's identity, and whether the data relates to NVIDIA are all unknown.

items.headline: N-able confirms unauthorised server access disrupts Mail Assure and SpamExperts management
items.summary: N-able says an attacker accessed one server in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud, disabling portal, APIs, quarantine and logging in three regions. Mail flow continues; no customer data compromise found so far.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: Vendor (affected party) acknowledged unauthorised server access; investigation ongoing. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 16 Nov 2026 (service disruption notice to customers); 18 Nov 2026 03:05 UTC security-incident disclosure via N-able status page, reported by The Hacker News on 19 Nov

sections.happened: N-able disclosed unauthorised access to one server in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud, which disabled the management portal and APIs across Americas, APAC and Europe. Mail flow and filtering continue. N-able says no evidence of customer data compromise yet. Restoration was ongoing as of 08:00 UTC on 19 Nov.
sections.technical: Attacker, entry method and access duration not disclosed. Portal, APIs, quarantine and logging are offline pending security validation. No CVEs or IOCs published. N-able says the incident is unrelated to the N-central vulnerabilities (Able2Shell and related names).
sections.guidance: N-able says it emailed partners with environment-specific information on whether action is required. Partners who did not receive that email should contact N-able Technical Support.
sections.differing: N-able first attributed the 16 Nov disruption to platform configuration and service dependencies, then revised this on 18 Nov to a security incident. Reports note no public confirmation of credential exposure.
sections.unknown: Attacker identity, intrusion method, duration, scope of data accessed, and restoration timeline are not publicly confirmed by N-able.

items.headline: TfL takes Oyster photocard website offline after account compromise affecting about 265,000 customers
items.summary: Transport for London says around 265,000 Oyster photocard customers may have had account details compromised after unauthorised emails prompted it to take the photocard site offline on 16 November. Passwords and payment data were reportedly not affected. The ICO was notified.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: TfL statement by named director, reported consistently by multiple outlets; ICO notified. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026 11:01 UK (The Register); TfL statement issued 18 Nov

sections.happened: TfL says it became aware on 16 November 2026 that Oyster photocard customers were receiving emails asking them to create accounts they already held. The emails came from TfL's own systems but resulted from the compromise. TfL took the photocard website down, contained the incident and says about 265,000 customers may have had account details compromised. Affected card types include Zip Oyster, 18+ Student, 18-25 Care Leaver, 60+ London, Apprentice and Veterans photocards. TfL informed the ICO and began emailing affected customers on 18 November. Existing cards still work; renewals and journey-history queries go through customer services. No restoration date given.
sections.technical: TfL has not disclosed how the attackers gained access. The observable indicator was unauthorised account-creation emails sent from TfL's own systems. A customer email reported by Greatest Hits Radio lists name, email, home address, phone number, date of birth and security question and answer as accessed. TfL's current assessment is that passwords, bank or payment card details, journey data and children's Zip Oyster names and dates of birth were not compromised. No CVE, actor, malware or IOCs published.
sections.guidance: TfL says it will ask all photocard customers to change their password, security question and answer, and advises changing the password on any other online service using the same details. It says customers can contact its Customer Services for renewals or journey history while the site is offline.
sections.differing: Reports differ slightly on data exposed: TfL's public statement stresses what was not compromised, while a customer email quoted by Greatest Hits Radio lists personal fields. These are consistent, not contradictory.
sections.unknown: Attack method, perpetrator, how many of the 265,000 accounts were actually accessed, and when the site returns are undisclosed. No evidence of misuse found so far, per TfL.

items.headline: Microsoft Agent Framework PyPI package compromised to steal credentials
items.summary: Malicious agent-framework releases 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 on PyPI ran a credential stealer at Python startup. PyPI quarantined both; 1.26.0 is the last clean release.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: PyPI quarantined both releases; Microsoft's repo issue acknowledges them as pulled; multiple security firms analysed the payloads.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (UK time) via BleepingComputer; first malicious upload 17 Nov 2026 20:35 UTC (GMT) per StepSecurity and Aikido

sections.happened: Versions 1.26.1 (uploaded 20:35 UTC, 17 Nov) and 1.26.2 (21:08 UTC) of Microsoft's agent-framework on PyPI carried a credential stealer. PyPI quarantined both. The package has about 190,000–200,000 monthly downloads. How the attacker gained publishing access is unknown.
sections.technical: Malicious .pth startup hook runs on every Python start, without importing the package (T1546-style startup persistence). Harvests env vars, .env and credential files, and requests Azure managed-identity and CI OIDC tokens. Exfiltrates to a webhook.site endpoint. 1.26.2 adds GitHub Actions OIDC and runner-directory harvesting. No CVE assigned.
sections.guidance: StepSecurity advises isolating affected hosts and runners before running Python or pip, rebuilding from a clean base, and pinning agent-framework to 1.26.0. Rotate stored secrets and review OIDC, federated and managed-identity permissions.
sections.differing: BleepingComputer says the attacker's access method is unclear; Microsoft has not responded to its query. Aikido and Wiz note possible upload outside the normal release process. StepSecurity says token requests are unconfirmed as issued.
sections.unknown: How publishing access was obtained, whether the upload credential is revoked, and whether any tokens were issued. Microsoft has not stated a point of breach.

items.headline: F5 patches six critical BIG-IP TMM flaws that can crash traffic and may allow RCE
items.summary: F5 disclosed six CVSS 9.8 stack-based buffer overflows in BIG-IP's data plane that let unauthenticated attackers crash TMM under specific configurations. Only engineering hotfixes fix them; no exploitation reported.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: F5 advisories published; details partly from search snippets, not full advisory pages. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (UK time not stated in sources); first source The Hacker News, F5 advisory K000163937

sections.happened: On 18 November 2026 F5 disclosed six BIG-IP flaws (CVE-2026-123637, -121805, -120292, -120285, -116953, -120722) that let an unauthenticated remote attacker terminate TMM, interrupting traffic until restart. F5 says they may also allow RCE. WatchTowr reported four; F5 found two. F5 reports no exploitation.
sections.technical: CWE-121 stack-based buffer overflows in the data plane, CVSS 3.1 9.8 and 4.0 9.3. Triggers require an iRule using a specific command (PEM::subscriber, MR::message route, PSC::ip_address, GENERICMESSAGE::route, DNS::scrape) or an APM per-request policy with Client Information and Endpoint Security agents.
sections.guidance: F5 lists engineering hotfixes as the only fix and no workaround. Fixed builds: BNK-2.4.2-EHF1, BNK-2.3.4-EHF1, BNK-2.2.5-EHF1; CNF-2.4.2-EHF1, CNF-2.3.4-EHF1, CNF-2.2.5-EHF1. Hotfixes carry no QA assessment or warranty per F5.
sections.differing: F5's advisory lists BIG-IP CNF as not vulnerable to CVE-2026-120722, but its CVE record lists CNF as affected. Treat as unresolved until F5 clarifies.
sections.unknown: No exploitation confirmed; RCE is described as possible only. Older unsupported releases are not evaluated. Fixed builds for BIG-IP proper not listed in the sources read.

items.headline: Perforce Puppet Enterprise RCE CVE-2026-115731 added to CISA KEV
items.summary: CISA added critical Puppet Server deserialization flaw CVE-2026-115731 (CVSS 9.4) to its KEV catalog on 17 November; federal deadline 1 December. Perforce says it knows of no attacks.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: CISA KEV listing records exploitation; vendor says it is unaware of attacks; attackers and scale unnamed. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 3 Nov 2026, c.20:40 UTC (CVE publication and Perforce fix); KEV listing 17 Nov reported by CybersecurityNews

sections.happened: Perforce fixed CVE-2026-115731 and CVE-2026-115732 on 3 November 2026. CISA added CVE-2026-115731 to its KEV catalog on 17 November, citing active exploitation, with a 1 December deadline for US federal agencies. Attackers and victim numbers are not public.
sections.technical: CWE-502 deserialization in Puppet Server report processing. A client with any CA-signed agent certificate sends a crafted rich-data report via HTTP PUT to run code as the Puppet Server service user. With autosign, an unauthenticated network attacker can obtain a certificate. CVSS 9.4 (Perforce); CVE-2026-115732 CVSS 9.0.
sections.guidance: Upgrade to Puppet Enterprise 2026.0.1, 2025.12.1 or 2023.8.13, or Puppet Core 9.1.3 or 8.22.2, then restart the server. Meanwhile review autosign configuration and authorization rules.
sections.differing: CISA's KEV listing records exploitation; Perforce says it is not aware of attacks and found no evidence of customer data being accessed. Trade reports describe the KEV listing as based on evidence of active exploitation.
sections.unknown: Threat actors, victim count, initial access details and in-the-wild IOCs were not published in the sources read.

items.headline: Broadcom patches critical vCenter authentication bypass CVE-2026-123890, exploited as zero-day per Mandiant
items.summary: Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0009 fixes CVE-2026-123890, a CVSS 9.8 vCenter authentication bypass with no workaround. Mandiant and GTIG report exploitation in early September 2026.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Broadcom advisory and Mandiant/GTIG report both published 19 Nov 2026; exploitation per Mandiant.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026, Broadcom advisory VMSA-2026-0009 and Google Cloud GTIG/Mandiant blog (same day, UK time not stated in sources)

sections.happened: Broadcom published VMSA-2026-0009 on 19 November 2026 for CVE-2026-123890, an authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service affecting vCenter, reported by Mandiant. Mandiant and GTIG said ARMORY CASTLE exploited it as a zero-day in early September 2026. Broadcom lists no workaround.
sections.technical: Unauthenticated SRP-6a session key disclosure over DCE/RPC on TCP 2012, exploiting predictable UUIDv1 timestamps. Yields an administrator@vsphere.local session. Mandiant says the BONESAW tool created SSO admin accounts and stole the SAML signing key and directory database. CVSS 9.8.
sections.guidance: Broadcom says apply the fixed vCenter builds (9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200, 8.0 U3m); no workaround is listed. Mandiant strongly recommends immediate patching. Broadcom says vSphere 7.0 needs extended support contract.
sections.differing: Trade press (The Hacker News) reported no known attacks; Mandiant/GTIG report exploitation in early September 2026. Mandiant's forensic account is the better-supported source.
sections.unknown: Full scope of victims and number of compromised systems not stated. Attribution to a China-linked actor appears only in secondary coverage.

items.labelBasis: Independent verification did not run for this top story, so the label is lowered; details come from the cited reports.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 (Apache advisory, as relayed by SecurityWeek); coverage 18 Nov 2026 by The Hacker News and Security Affairs

sections.happened: On 17 November 2026 Apache published CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 9.8) for Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 and said it is being actively exploited, without naming targets or actors. It is the same bug as CVE-2026-82384, disclosed in September for 6.1.5 only. Separately, SecurityWeek reports Axis 1.x flaw CVE-2026-90436 (CVSS 9.8, disclosed 6 November) is exploited; CISA added it to KEV with a 21 November deadline.
sections.technical: Roller's XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester (unauthenticated, remote code execution). Corgea states an unauthenticated POST to /roller-services/xmlrpc can carry a serialized Java object and that a public PoC has existed since 28 September. Axis: unsafe reflection in end-of-life Axis 1.x; Rapid7 saw exploitation on 13 November against Confluence Data Center, with database access and a later Microsoft 365 sign-in; N-central also affected.
sections.guidance: Apache: upgrade to Roller 6.1.6 or later, or set enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping, then restart. Disabling XML-RPC in the admin UI is not enough. Axis: no fixed 1.x release; Apache advises migrating or applying its patch. Confluence 9.2.28; N-central 2026.4 HF3.
sections.unknown: Who is exploiting Roller, how many instances are compromised and who is targeted are undisclosed. Whether Previdian's Axis attempts succeeded is not established. The original Apache advisory was not read directly.

items.headline: CISA adds four exploited flaws to KEV: Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis, REDCap
items.summary: CISA added four vulnerabilities to its KEV catalog on 18 November 2026 citing active exploitation: Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and Vanderbilt REDCap. Federal deadlines are set.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: CISA KEV catalog alert names the four CVEs as actively exploited.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (US date), CISA alert; The Hacker News followed the same day

sections.happened: CISA added CVE-2024-10441 (Synology DSM), CVE-2026-40217 (BerriAI LiteLLM), CVE-2026-90436 (Apache Axis) and CVE-2026-90817 (Vanderbilt REDCap) to its KEV catalog on 18 November 2026, citing active exploitation. Federal agencies were given deadlines of 21 November (DSM, REDCap, Axis) and 2 December (LiteLLM).
sections.technical: CVE-2026-90436 (CVSS 9.8) unsafe reflection in Apache Axis 1.x, unauthenticated RCE; Rapid7 saw it used against Confluence Data Center with Remote API enabled. CVE-2026-90817 (CVSS 9.8) code injection in REDCap via public survey context. CVE-2026-40217 (CVSS 8.8) LiteLLM bytecode rewriting at /guardrails/test_custom_code. CVE-2024-10441 (CVSS 9.8) Synology DSM, linked to C3RB3R ransomware.
sections.guidance: CISA: agencies must apply fixes or mitigations under BOD 26-04; all organisations encouraged to prioritise KEV entries. Atlassian: Confluence is vulnerable only if Remote API (XML-RPC & SOAP) is enabled. Axis 1 is end-of-life; migrate to Axis 2 or a patched build.
sections.differing: The Hacker News reports Rapid7 linked CVE-2026-90436 to Confluence intrusions and Safe Security reported XMRig miners via CVE-2026-90817. Both are third-party reports cited by the outlet, not CISA findings.
sections.unknown: CVE-2026-90436 has no vendor patch since Axis 1 is end-of-life. Patch status for LiteLLM and REDCap and full exploitation scope were not confirmed in the sources read.

items.headline: Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 exploited after public PoC, F6 reports Russian victim
items.summary: F6 says attackers used critical Cisco Expressway flaw CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8) to breach a Russian organisation soon after a public PoC appeared. Cisco's advisory still says it knows of no malicious use; clustered devices only, fixed in X15.5.20.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: Exploitation reported by F6 only; Cisco advisory unrevised, no actor attributed.
items.firstReported: SecurityWeek, article dated around 19 Nov 2026 (time not stated); based on F6 report

sections.happened: Cisco published advisory cisco-sa-vcs-static-cred-hr7EWZ8t on 21 October 2026 for CVE-2026-76466 in Expressway Series. SecurityWeek reports a PoC was later posted on GitHub and that security firm F6 investigated an intrusion at an unnamed Russian organisation shortly afterwards. Attackers compromised two internet-exposed X15.5.3 devices, then two internal cluster nodes. F6 did not attribute the attack. Cisco had not revised its advisory.
sections.technical: Flaw (CWE-798, CVSS 9.8) lies in the database service: persistent cookies plus unvalidated client certificates in clustering let an unauthenticated attacker invoke RPC commands and run commands as root. Only clustered Expressway-C/E affected. After root, attackers used custom Python scripts for network scanning, SMB, SQL Server, WinRM and GitLab searches, which F6 says showed signs of AI-assistant use. Detection: Erlang system log. F6 published IPs and file paths.
sections.guidance: Cisco: upgrade to X15.5.20; X14 and earlier must migrate; no workarounds. F6, for those unable to patch: block TCP 4371–4372 except from trusted cluster nodes.
sections.differing: Cisco's advisory says it is unaware of malicious use; F6 reports exploitation. The advisory predates the report and had not been revised.
sections.unknown: Victim identity, actor, PoC author and source, how attackers obtained the cookies, and Cisco's response remain unstated.

items.headline: Drupal patches critical installer RCE CVE-2026-132165; exploits expected
items.summary: Drupal core fixed CVE-2026-132165, a critical installer flaw allowing anonymous site takeover or RCE under specific conditions. A proof-of-concept exists; no attacks reported.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Drupal Security Team advisory SA-CORE-2026-017 published; fixed releases available.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 17:43 UTC (drupal.org advisory SA-CORE-2026-017); advance notice 16 Nov

sections.happened: The Drupal Security Team released fixes on 18 November 2026 for CVE-2026-132165 in install.php, rated Critical (18/25). Under specific conditions an anonymous attacker can attempt a site reinstall, leading to takeover or RCE. Fixed in 10.6.22, 11.3.22 and 11.4.13.
sections.technical: Flaw in Drupal core install.php; found by Anthropic's OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-GMRPK0BU). Exploitation rated complex; a proof-of-concept exists. Some paths blocked if web server cannot write to settings.php. Affects Drupal below 10.6.22 and 11.0.0 to below 11.3.22 and 11.4.0 to below 11.4.13.
sections.guidance: Upgrade to 11.4.13, 11.3.22 or 10.6.22. Sites that cannot upgrade should follow Drupal's installer-securing guidance, such as blocking /core/install.php. Drupal Steward protects known vectors; upgrade still advised.
sections.differing: Drupal says exploit paths are uncommon and complex, while the Security Team warned exploits could appear within hours or days. The advisory reports no attacks in the wild.
sections.unknown: Whether exploitation has occurred in production is not reported. Full list of conditions needed for exploitation is not public.

items.headline: Java4Shell: OpenJDK Base64 flaw CVE-2026-114938 patched; exploitation attempts begin
items.summary: Calif disclosed a memory-corruption bug in OpenJDK's AVX-512 Base64 decoder on 17 November; Oracle and OpenJDK patched the same day. Scanning and blind exploit attempts began by 19 November; no confirmed compromises reported.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Oracle/OpenJDK advisory, CISA, multiple vendors; exploitation attempts seen by GreyNoise, watchTowr.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026, evening UK (Calif write-up; OpenJDK/Oracle patch released 1pm PT)

sections.happened: Calif disclosed Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) on 17 November 2026; Oracle and OpenJDK released patches at 1pm PT that day. Infosecurity Magazine reports some details leaked before coordinated disclosure. CISA issued an emergency advisory. SecurityWeek reports GreyNoise saw 150+ matching requests from five IPs by early 19 November, and watchTowr and Previdian saw exploitation attempts; none confirmed successful. Cisco, Siemens, Elastic, Red Hat, Atlassian and Keycloak published advisories; Amazon, Microsoft and Azul shipped patched builds.
sections.technical: Out-of-bounds heap write in HotSpot's x86-64 Base64 intrinsic, which uses AVX-512 VBMI: the store mask for the padded tail is miscalculated, so a 65-character input (64 'A' plus '=') overwrites 62 bytes past the array. Affects OpenJDK 17, 21, 25 and 27; ARM is unaffected. Oracle rates CVSS v3.1 8.1; Calif rates CVSS v4.0 9.2. Calif says no universal exploit exists; each application needs a bespoke chain.
sections.guidance: Calif: update immediately, or start the JVM with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics or -XX:UseAVX=2 (x86-64 only). CISA: inventory bundled Java runtimes, patch internet-facing systems first, validate and limit Base64 input, and watch for JVM crashes. Atlassian advises disabling AVX-512 for Data Center products.
sections.differing: Oracle scores the flaw High (8.1, CVSS v3.1) while Calif scores it Critical (9.2, CVSS v4.0). VulnCheck, Endor Labs and Calif all describe exploitation as hardware-specific and application-specific.
sections.unknown: Whether any intrusions have succeeded; Cisco and Siemens fixes are pending, and Cisco is still checking IOS XE and UCS Central.

items.headline: F5 patches five critical NGINX 'nginx2root' flaws; HTTP/2 RCE has public PoCs
items.summary: F5 fixed five NGINX memory-corruption flaws rated CVSS 4.0 9.2, led by CVE-2026-123007 in HTTP/2, present since 1.9.5. Public proof-of-concept code exists. No exploitation in the wild reported; code execution needs ASLR bypass.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: Independent verification did not run for this top story, so the label is lowered; details come from the cited reports.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (UK time not stated): The Hacker News; F5 advisories published same day

sections.happened: On 18 November 2026 F5 released NGINX Open Source 1.30.7 and 1.31.9 and NGINX Plus 37.0.8.1 and 37.3.0.1, fixing five flaws dubbed nginx2root, plus 17 other issues across its products. The lead flaw, CVE-2026-123007, affects HTTP/2 in every open-source release from 1.9.5 to 1.31.8. Researchers at Xint, Wiz, Ikotas Labs, Metnir and Rapid7 reported them. Rapid7 and Censys published PoC code. F5 reports no exploitation; Censys estimated about 8.8 million potentially exposed services.
sections.technical: CVE-2026-123007: HTTP/2 flow-control memory corruption. Others: CVE-2026-123633 (HTTP/2 use-after-free, proxying), CVE-2026-123634 (resolver use-after-free, SSI/mirror subrequests), CVE-2026-121810 (HTTP/3 use-after-free), CVE-2026-113425 (mail proxy). F5 scores all five CVSS 4.0 9.2; code execution requires ASLR disabled or bypassed. Rapid7's exploit needs about 128 GB of HTTP/2 traffic; Xint chained the flaw with a Linux SCTP kernel bug for container escape and root. Code runs as the worker process.
sections.guidance: F5 and NGINX: upgrade to 1.30.7/1.31.9 or Plus 37.0.8.1/37.3.0.1. Workarounds exist for only two flaws: avoid SSI/mirror with variable-based proxied names; restrict mail proxy listeners. CIRCL, per The Hacker News, lists disabling HTTP/2 as a temporary mitigation for two flaws.
sections.differing: Xint reported 98.9% of version-disclosing hosts in the affected range; researcher Florian Roth says exposure needs HTTP/2 and non-default setups, so version counts overstate risk. Censys reproduced memory corruption without Rapid7's traffic volume but did not achieve RCE, per BleepingComputer.
sections.unknown: Whether exploitation has begun is unconfirmed. Real-world exposure after configuration and distro backports is unclear; Ubuntu and Debian fixes were pending on 18 November.

items.headline: PHP security release fixes multiple critical RCE flaws, including PHP2Shell-related bugs
items.summary: PHP released 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13 and 8.6.0 fixing several CVSS 9.2 flaws, including CVE-2026-115560 and a session-file deserialization bug. Exploitation depends on non-default configurations.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Release announced by PHP; primary release notes unread; details from press and a secondary write-up. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (PHP pre-release notice, per DEV Community); release 19 Nov 2026, 14:00-14:30 UK time, per SecurityWeek

sections.happened: The PHP Foundation released security updates on 19 November 2026 for all supported branches. The Hacker News lists seven critical flaws, mostly CVSS 9.2, including CVE-2026-115560 and session-handling bugs. Fixes landed in PHP 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, 8.5.13 and 8.6.0.
sections.technical: CVE-2026-126714 ("phpAfterShell", Depthfirst): interrupted session write can leave a malformed session file, giving a deserialization primitive. Needs a gadget chain and file-based sessions. CVE-2026-115560 needs a non-default session configuration.
sections.guidance: PHP advises upgrading promptly to the fixed releases. If patching is not possible, turn off session upload progress, per The Hacker News and PHP's earlier advisory.
sections.differing: PHP's October advisory said CVE-2026-115560 was not fixed by its 21 October releases; the 19 November releases fix it. Fixed-version lists differ between CVEs; check each.
sections.unknown: Primary PHP release notes were not read. Exploitation status of the new CVEs is not reported. Full CVE lists beyond the press listings are unverified.

items.headline: Ukraine and FBI arrest four suspects tied to $40.5M in ransomware payments
items.summary: Ukrainian police, working with the FBI, detained four key members of a ransomware extortion group that police say received over $40.5M from at least 28 companies.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Acknowledged by Ukrainian National Police and Prosecutor General's Office; ransom figures are police claims.
items.firstReported: 18 November 2026, 10:30 UK time (12:30 Kyiv), Censor.NET interview with National Police acting chief

sections.happened: Ukrainian police with the FBI conducted 66 searches in Kyiv and 11 regions and detained four key suspects, who have been notified of suspicion and are in custody. Police say at least 27 members operate from Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Russia and other countries, within a network of more than 60. At least 28 companies paid over $40.5M.
sections.technical: Social engineering: attackers impersonated IT support by phone, used AI-generated voice messages, phishing pages mimicking corporate VPNs, and TeamViewer or AnyDesk. They stole data, encrypted systems and extorted cryptocurrency. Court records name Chaos ransomware; police did not name the strain.
sections.differing: Court records reported by LeMagIT and The Record name Chaos ransomware; police have not named a strain. Conti or BlackSuit links for the suspects remain unconfirmed.
sections.unknown: Full damages still being established. Suspects' identities, arrest locations and Conti links are unconfirmed. Ransom totals are police figures. Other members are still being sought.

items.headline: US interim rule requires licences for advanced AI chips to Southeast Asian data centres serving Chinese firms
items.summary: A US Commerce interim rule reported on 17–18 November requires licences for advanced AI chip exports to data centres in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. China calls it coercion; Alibaba and Tencent shares fell.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: Independent verification did not run for this top story, so the label is lowered; details come from the cited reports.
items.firstReported: Monday 17 November 2026 (NBC News, BIS announcement); CNBC 18 November

sections.happened: The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule requiring licences to export, re-export or transfer advanced AI chips to data centres in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, per The Diplomat. Data centres with large Chinese customers must apply within 90 days, per CNBC via DigitalToday. US-linked operators are exempt. Alibaba shares fell 5% and Tencent 3%, per Quartz citing Reuters; Malaysian operators fell sharply. Tencent said the rule sets everyone back, per The Register headline.
sections.guidance: Malaysia's trade minister said Kuala Lumpur does not intend to negotiate and expects operators to comply. Singapore said it is studying the measure and engaging affected companies. Thailand's deputy commerce minister said it would monitor chip imports and consult the US.
sections.differing: China's Foreign Ministry called the rules economic coercion and promised necessary measures, per the BBC via Quartz. The US framing, per reports, is closing a loophole letting Chinese firms reach restricted chips through foreign data centres.
sections.unknown: The Federal Register text and licence criteria were not read. Final scope, the Brazil provisions and any Chinese retaliation remain unclear.

items.headline: Anthropic prices record $81.3bn Nasdaq IPO at $83 a share, ~$1.5tn valuation
items.summary: Anthropic sold 980 million shares at $83, above its $70–78 range, raising $81.3bn, a record IPO. With a $26bn private placement the total is about $107bn. Trading on Nasdaq as ANT began 19 November.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Reported consistently by CBS, CNBC, Bloomberg and Semafor; filing itself not read. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: Pricing announced Wednesday 18 November 2026 (US); CNBC report, exact UK time not shown

sections.happened: Anthropic PBC priced its IPO on 18 November at $83 a share, above the $70–78 range, and upsized it from a planned 825 million shares to 980 million. CBS News and CNBC report proceeds of $81.3bn, exceeding SpaceX's $75bn June IPO. CBS reports a roughly $1.5tn valuation. Further placements to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Microsoft and Nvidia bring the total to about $107bn. Trading under ANT on Nasdaq began on 19 November; CBS reported the Nasdaq up 1.9% in early trading. Bloomberg reported grey-market indications of a first-day gain of more than 20%.
sections.unknown: First-day closing price, final allotment details and the SEC prospectus terms were not read; grey-market and perpetual-futures premiums are indications only.
